language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi! My name is Chip.
Ciao, my friends. My name is a Marco, and I work at my uncle Leone’s pizza shop. I help make pizzas.
Round pizzas are boring, so I try making other flat shapes like these.
Sometimes just for fun, I make three-dimensional, or 3-D, shapes from the pizza pieces – like this!
Look—I made a square pyramid! My teacher told me a pyramid get its name from the shape of its base,
and it has triangular faces, which all meet at one point.
I can do the same thing to build a prism. I learned a prism is made with two matching bases and rectangular faces.
Pyramids and prisms come in a number of different forms and styles—each with faces, edges, and corners.
When you cut the shape from side to side, you see the cross section. This looks just like the base—only smaller.
When I cut the pyramid from top to bottom down the middle, the cross section is a triangle—just like one of the faces.
Phew! I’m getting tired. I hope you can help me finish my homework.
